main_text.l: les se reddebát. Peccato enim & præuarica-
tione nondum præsente, gloria, quæ super-
nè venerat, vestiti erant: & quasi angeli ver-
sabantur in paradiso, non concupiscentijs
flagrantes, non ab aliis affectionibus infesta-
ti, non naturæ necessitatibus obnoxij: sed
prorsus incorruptibiles & immortales con-
diti, neque vel vestimentorum amictu ibi e-
gebant, ut Chrysostomus scribit. Præclarus
sane fructus innocentiæ est bene sibi conscia
nuditas, & animus pudoris nescius. Ac quo-
niam hodie videmus neq; pueros ex iua nu-
ditate erubescere, demus operam ut quoque
simus pueri, non quidem sensibus, sed mali-
tia, ne pudefiamus, quando cuique reddet se
cundum opera sua Dominus Iesus, qui disci-
pulis suis dixit, Matthæi decimo octauo: A-
men dico vobis, nisi conuersi fueritis, & effi-
ciamini sicut pueri, non ingrediemini in re-
gnum cœlorum: de cuius possessione vti-
nam nostrūm nullus depellatur, Amen.
CONCIO II.
Genes. 3.

page.notes: Printing errors left as printed: "iua" (ex iua nud, for sua?) and "neq;" with its abbreviation mark. The word "nostrūm" is doubtful: the mark over the u is hard to read and may be a different abbreviation. Long s in "s" forms and the "ćtauo" accent on the c in "octauo" are scan artefacts and were written plainly. The signature "B s[?]" is uncertain. The paragraph ends mid-word "& i-" and continues on the next page. Printed "Genes. 3." is a verse reference and was set as level 3.
